messages:
jamie: heads up — my canary rollout for v2-fastpath just started showing elevated 5xx on the /v1/generate route. saw it at ~04:12 UTC. pattern looks like healthcheck failures then spikes in 500s. paging oncall now :rotating_light:
incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED — Canary health probe failures (thread 1897654321). Severity: P1. Triggers: canary-probe > 2% 5xx over 5m, healthcheck failing on 3/4 hosts. Paging oncall.
deploy-bot: Deploy started: rollout/v2-fastpath@jamie -> 15% canary (8 hosts). Deploy ID: dep-2026-07-12-1345.
ravi: oncall here. looking at metrics — error rate peaked at 3.4% on generation, request rate ~1.2k rps for the canary slice. Which config changed in this rollout?
jamie: added a connection pool tweak to low-latency mode + small kv-cache change (TTL lowered). thought it was safe.
olivia: logs show 502s with traceback in proxy: upstream read timeout followed by 500 on runtime. attaching sample logs: ```[2026-07-12T04:14:03Z] gen-node-5 ERROR rpc timeout reading stream -> downstream 502
[2026-07-12T04:14:04Z] gen-node-5 ERROR task failed: kvcache-miss + pool-refused```
maria: feature flag is rollout.v2_fastpath=true for canary. can toggle to false to stop canary early.
ravi: ok first priority: stop customer impact. jamie, can you hit the abort flag (kill-switch) for this rollout? we have abort criteria met (5xx > 2.5% for 5m).
jamie: setting abort now — toggling flag: `curl -X POST https://console/api/flags/rollout.v2_fastpath -d '{"value":false}'` -> response 200. deploy-bot: Canary abort acknowledged: rollout/v2-fastpath paused and new traffic redirected to stable.
incident-bot: ACTION: Canary aborted by jamie (reason: elevated 5xx). Auto-fallback to stable model variant initiated.
olivia: after abort, 5xx dropped back under 0.4% within 90s. latency back to baseline.
maria: customer impact assessment: preliminary — about 0.7% of requests across region experienced errors during the 6m window; top affected customers: beta-testers (app IDs a-112, b-77). No broad SLA breaches reported yet.
ravi: good. next steps: (1) collect a few failing traces and minimal repro, (2) roll back the connection-pool tweak in a staging branch, (3) run targeted smoke on a small internal canary with synthetic load. jamie can you grab traces?
jamie: grabbing traces now; shipping sample to #incidents-s3 (link: https://s3.redwood/internal/incidents/1897654321/traces.tar.gz).
olivia: quick note — gen-node-5 had sporadic file-descriptor exhaustion in the logs right before the 502s. patch candidate: increase max_fds and add backpressure on the queue.
maria: tagging infra to review limits — @ravi @olivia pls coordinate.
ravi: passing to afternoon oncall (maria) for followup and retro. maria, you taking handoff?
maria: taking handoff. I’ll run the rollback in staging, validate, then schedule a controlled re-rollout after fixes. posting incident timeline to the ops doc.
incident-bot: PAGING: On-call handoff recorded — ravi -> maria. Handoff notes: canary aborted, artifacts at s3, potential fd exhaustion in gen-node, patch and controlled re-rollout required.
jamie: retro notes: probably we were too aggressive on pool trimming. will draft a config-change checklist to include fd headroom checks.
olivia: adding hypothesis to the post-incident doc: combination of lower TTL + pool trim caused pool thrash under bursty load, leading to upstream timeouts.
maria: customer comms: recommend no immediate broad notification — limited impact to beta clusters. If we see any downstream error upticks in next 24h or replay shows user-facing errors >1% for paid customers, escalate to comms.
ravi: leaving a couple of followups assigned: 1) jamie - open PR to revert pool change and include fds check, 2) olivia - run stress test harness simulating burst-to-pool, 3) infra - add fd alerting for gen nodes. please update the incident doc with owners.
jamie: PR created: https://git.redwood/pulls/3242 (revert pool change). CI green.
olivia: stress test note: reproduce locally with `wrk -t12 -c600 -d120s http://canary/v1/generate` and watch fd count.
maria: final status: mitigation complete, canary aborted, impact limited. moving to postmortem stage. adding labels: canary-failure, abort, rollback candidate.
incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated -> monitoring. If errors resurface, reopen.
ravi: thanks team. leaving oncall slack thread.
maria: copying summary to #product-ops and scheduling a 30m postmortem at 09:00 UTC. everyone add notes. :thumbsup:
